caution: A failure to reproduce is not a finding that the paper is wrong. It may be a failure of the attempt.

attempts.label: ZENODO:3924718
attempts.entry_title: Coupling of the gastric mill and pyloric rhythms across temperature (Powell et al. 2021)
attempts.summary: Most of the paper's findings on evoked rhythms hold in this data: gastric mill and pyloric periods shorten with temperature in all 10 preparations, their Q10s do not differ, and LG stays integer-coupled to PD from 7 to 21 C while DG does not. Two did not reproduce: a Q10 of about 2 in most preparations (1 of 10 by the Methods' formula; the paper's count follows its code's per-burst Q10), and a drop in LG spiking near the PD burst end at higher temperatures. LG phase locking held in part. The spontaneous rhythms from 11 to 30 C and the rhythm without the pyloric pacemaker could not be tested, as those recordings are not in the deposit.
attempts.description: Tests the findings of Powell, Haddad, Gorur-Shandilya and Marder (2021) on Zenodo record 3924718, which holds the spike times, temperature and stimulation mask of the ten preparations in which gastric mill rhythms were evoked, and raw recordings. It tests the temperature dependence of the LG and PD burst periods, their Q10s, the slowing after stimulation, integer coupling of LG and DG with PD, and the phase of LG and DG in the PD cycle. The spontaneous recordings and those with the pyloric pacemaker hyperpolarized are not in the record.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Powell et al. (2021) from Zenodo record 3924718

outcomes.statement: Spontaneous gastric mill activity (LG bursting) occurred at temperatures between 11 and 30 C, in nine preparations in total.
outcomes.source: Results, Spontaneous gastric mill rhythms span a physiological range of temperatures, paragraphs 1 and 3; Figure 2 and Figure 2, figure supplement 1
outcomes.quote: We inspected a dataset of extracellular recordings of dgn and lgn during temperature ramps ( Haddad and Marder, 2018 ) and found spontaneous gastric mill activity at temperatures between 11°C and 30°C ... there were a total of nine preparations in which spontaneous rhythms were observed at a variety of different temperatures
outcomes.notes: The nine preparations with spontaneous rhythms (crabs of July 2013, recordings of Haddad and Marder 2018) are not in the record. Its only spike annotations, evoked_data.mat, are the ten evoked preparations of getEvokedData.m, and its zips hold raw files of nine of those ten and of 941_003 and 941_006, recorded in June 2019. The paper's data statement names only this record. A search of Zenodo (queries on Haddad, Marder, Powell, stomatogastric, temperature) and DANDI (stomatogastric) found no deposit of them; Zenodo record 5139650 (Haddad and Marder) holds six ABF files of notebooks 845 and 857 recorded in the decentralized condition, with no spike annotations and not the example preparation 830_116.

outcomes.statement: In the example preparation of Figure 2a, spontaneous gastric mill rhythms were relatively regular at lower temperatures and less regular at higher temperatures.
outcomes.source: Results, Spontaneous gastric mill rhythms span a physiological range of temperatures, paragraph 2; Figure 2a
outcomes.quote: While these recordings show relatively regular gastric mill rhythms at lower temperatures, they were less regular at higher temperatures
outcomes.notes: The example preparation 830_116_2 belongs to the spontaneous set, which is not in the record (see fig2-spontaneous-11-to-30).

outcomes.statement: Gastric mill rhythms could be evoked by dpon stimulation across 7 to 21 C in 9 of 10 preparations.
outcomes.source: Results, Gastric mill rhythms speed up with increased temperature, paragraph 1; Figure 3
outcomes.quote: We were able to evoke gastric rhythms across a temperature range of 7 to 21°C in 9 of 10 preparations
outcomes.notes: Under reading (a) (at least one LG burst period in a bin), 9 of 10 preparations have an LG rhythm at every bin from 7 to 21 C they were held at, under both burst rules, as the criterion is worded (every bin the preparation was held at). The one that fails is 901_086, which spent 330 s in the 21 C bin, with 70 s of stimulation there, and has no LG spike in it; its warmest LG burst start is at 19.1 C. 901_062 never reaches 21 C: its last stimulation is at 19.0 C, followed by 113 LG bursts and cooling back to about 7 C, so 21 C was never tried; it passes because it has a rhythm at every step it had (7, 11, 15 and 19 C), which fits the Methods' 'in some preparations, 19 C was the warmest temperature that a gastric mill rhythm could be evoked'. If 21 C must also be reached, 8 of 10 pass, which would not be reproduced. Under reading (b) (at least 30 significands) 2 of 10. All ten preparations are in the record (10 of 10 evoked). Counting every bin the temperature passed through gives 3 (reading a) and 1 (reading b) of 10, because the 9, 13 and 17 C bins crossed on ramps (20 to 270 s) have few or no LG bursts, so the outcome rests on the 120 s reading of held.
deviations: The claims file leaves open which bins a preparation 'was held at'. A bin counts as held when the recording spends at least 120 s in it, the 2-minute minimum step of the Methods ('a given temperature step was held for at least 2 minutes') and the code's (BurstPeriodsVsTime.m, 'temperature held for less than 2 minutes'). Counting every bin with any time in it gives 3 of 10, so the outcome rests on this choice, which is an assumption (assumed: true); the question is put to the paper's authors as a methods_unavailable finding.

A preparation whose warmest held bin is 19 C (901_062) passes when it has a rhythm at every bin it was held at, as the criterion is worded; the count requiring 21 C as well (8 of 10) is shown beside it.

outcomes.statement: In 4 of 10 evoked preparations a spontaneous gastric mill rhythm was seen at 11 C before stimulation; in three of these four the spontaneous and evoked rhythms were similar in LG spike and burst timing and in cycle period.
outcomes.source: Results, Gastric mill rhythms speed up with increased temperature, paragraph 2; Figure 3, figure supplement 1
outcomes.quote: Three of the four preparations that had spontaneous and evoked rhythms shared similarities in LG spike and burst timing ( Figure 3—figure supplement 1b ) and rhythm cycle period (mean ± SD; Figure 3—figure supplement 1c )
outcomes.notes: Tested on three of the four preparations of fig_within_prep_spont_evoked_comparison.m; 941_006 has no spike times in the record (941_006.zip holds raw ABF files and crabsort classifier files only). Spontaneous stretch file 0000, evoked files 0032, 0012 and 0020 as the script selects. Methods burst rule, LG period mean plus or minus SD; 901_086 24.0 +- 0.7 s (two periods) against 11.2 +- 2.9 s, 901_080 16.1 +- 6.9 s against 15.6 +- 2.9 s, 901_062 16.6 +- 5.7 s against 7.5 +- 0.8 s. Only 901_080 is similar under either reading, so the four can give at most two similar whatever 941_006 shows, and the criterion (three of four) fails. The code's burst rule gives the same. The script's own call (computePeriods with its default of 1 ISI, bursts of at least 2 spikes) gives 901_062 9.9 +- 3.5 s, similar under reading (b), which would leave three of four possible; that is a variant. Among the ten evoked preparations, 3 (901_062, 901_080, 901_086) have LG burst periods before their first stimulation in the 11 C bin (13 to 43 periods), not 4; 932_151 has 16 before stimulation at 9.83 to 9.93 C, just outside the bin, so with it 4 of 10 have pre-stimulation bursting; the fourth preparation of the paper's script is 941_006, which is not one of the ten. The first measured value is that count, the second the similar preparations of the three tested. Taking every pre-stimulation LG period at 11 C as the spontaneous stretch gives 21.7 +- 5.3, 17.5 +- 7.8 and 16.2 +- 4.9 s, the same picture. The evoked file the script selects for 901_080 (0012) is at 7.25 C, against 10.86 C for its spontaneous file; the comparison follows the script. The ISIs are shown and not judged, as the criterion sets.
deviations: 941_006 has no spike times in the record, so three of the four preparations are tested; the outcome does not depend on it under the Methods burst rule, since one similar of three allows at most two of four.
The spike times of a raw file are those within its samples in evoked_data.mat (the filename categorical), the stacked form of the same crabsort annotations the script reads per file.

outcomes.statement: Both LG (gastric mill) and PD (pyloric) burst periods decrease with increasing temperature, a coordinated decrease seen in all 10 preparations.
outcomes.source: Results, Gastric mill and pyloric cycle periods are similarly temperature-sensitive, paragraphs 1 and 2; Figure 4a and 4b
outcomes.quote: A coordinated decrease in both gastric mill and pyloric cycle periods was observed in all 10 preparations ( Figure 4b )
outcomes.notes: In all 10 preparations the mean PD and LG periods in the warmest bin are below those in the coldest (PD 0.77 to 2.00 s at 7 C against 0.28 to 0.56 s at the warmest; LG 12.5 to 40.2 s against 5.0 to 12.6 s), and the Spearman correlation of bin means with temperature is negative for both (PD -0.976 to -1, LG -0.643 to -1). The same holds under the code's burst rule.

outcomes.statement: Most preparations (8 of 10) had a cycle period Q10 of about 2 for both the pyloric and the gastric mill rhythm.
outcomes.source: Results, Gastric mill and pyloric cycle periods are similarly temperature-sensitive, paragraph 2; Figure 4c
outcomes.quote: Figure 4c shows that most preparations (8 of 10) exhibited a cycle period Q 10 of ~2 for both the pyloric and gastric mill rhythms
outcomes.notes: Under the Methods' Q10 over every bin, 1 of 10 preparations has both Q10s within 1.8 to 2.2 and 2 of 10 within 1.5 to 2.5; over the held steps only, 1 and 3 of 10. Per-preparation LG Q10s reach 16.6 and 39.0 when every bin is used, from bins at 9 and 13 C crossed during ramps (per-bin LG Q10s up to 98.7 and 180.8). The code's per-burst Q10 (variant) gives 3 of 10 within 1.8 to 2.2 and 8 of 10 within 1.5 to 2.5 (Methods burst rule; 1 and 8 with the code's), so the paper's count matches the code's computation under the wider reading of "~2". With T and T_11 the mean measured temperatures of the bursts in each bin in place of the bin centres (the verifier's point), the counts are the same (1 and 2 of 10 over every bin, 1 and 3 over the held steps). The per-preparation LG Q10s from every bin then reach 705 (901_052) and 70 (901_086), from the 9 C bin of each, which holds one LG burst, at 9.81 C against 10.89 C at 11 C (per-bin Q10 4919) and at 9.24 C against 11.03 C (335). Whether the code's Q10, which the paper's own t-test matches exactly, should be the main analysis is asked of a reader (questions/powell-2021.yaml).
deviations: The claims file does not say which temperatures enter the Methods' Q10. Two readings were run, every bin with bursts and only the bins held at least 120 s (the temperature steps of the Methods, "Spontaneous and evoked gastric mill rhythm temperature ranges"); both give the same outcome. T is the bin centre, f_T the mean of 1/period over bursts starting in the bin.
PD periods above 5 s and LG periods above 50 s are removed before the Q10, as fig_burst_period.m does (the outlier filter the claims file cites for fig4b-periods-decrease-all-preps).

outcomes.statement: The apparent Q10s of the pyloric (PD) and gastric mill (LG) burst frequencies do not differ (paired t-test, p = 0.235, N = 10, t = 1.27).
outcomes.source: Results, Gastric mill and pyloric cycle periods are similarly temperature-sensitive, paragraph 2; Figure 4c legend
outcomes.quote: Estimated Q 10 s were not significantly different for LG and PD burst periods (paired t-test, p = 0.235 , N = 10 , t = 1.27 )
outcomes.notes: Paired t-test on the Methods' Q10s (every bin), t = -1.418, p = 0.190, n = 10, mean PD minus LG -5.35 (driven by the two large LG Q10s); held steps only, t = -0.739, p = 0.479. The code's per-burst Q10 gives t = 1.204, p = 0.259 with the Methods burst rule and t = 1.272, p = 0.235 with the code's, the paper's values. No version reaches p < 0.05.

outcomes.statement: The evoked gastric mill rhythm slows down (LG burst period lengthens) with time since stimulation.
outcomes.source: Results, Gastric mill and pyloric cycle periods are similarly temperature-sensitive, paragraph 1; Figure 4, figure supplement 1
outcomes.quote: despite significant variability in the LG burst period, due to a slowing down ( Figure 4—figure supplement 1 ) of the gastric mill rhythm with time since stimulation
outcomes.notes: 64 stretches from 10 preparations. The slope of the mean LG period on time is positive at 8 of 9 temperatures under both burst rules (code's 7 ISIs and the Methods' 5 spikes), negative only at 13 C (-0.0006 s per s, two stretches). At 7, 11, 15, 19 and 21 C (8 to 17 stretches) the slopes are 0.0055 to 0.0171 s per s, r 0.63 to 0.87, and the mean period rises from 6.7 to 15.4 s in the first minute to 10.1 to 19.6 s at 9 to 10 minutes. No stretch has an even rounded temperature, so the odd-bin filter drops none.
deviations: A stimulation block is taken as running to the end of the recording when no stimulation follows, as MATLAB's temperature(stim:[]) is empty in BurstPeriodsVsTime.m; the mask's meaning (stimulation where 0) is taken from the code (findStimulationTimes.m, BurstPeriodsVsTime.m), as the record does not describe it.

outcomes.statement: With the pyloric pacemaker suppressed by hyperpolarizing both PD neurons, an evoked gastric mill rhythm persists, and its cycle period decreases with increasing temperature as it does with the pacemaker active.
outcomes.source: Results, Gastric mill rhythms can be evoked when the pyloric pacemaker is suppressed, paragraph 2; Figure 4, figure supplement 2c
outcomes.quote: Figure 4—figure supplement 2c shows that the gastric mill rhythm cycle period steadily decreased with increased temperature regardless of pyloric pacemaker activity
outcomes.notes: The nine preparations with the PD neurons hyperpolarized (2020, including 999_017 of PD_hyp.m) are not in the record; no zip or annotation carries a 999 notebook number, and the two preparations not among the evoked ten (941_003, 941_006) were recorded in June 2019.

outcomes.statement: In all nine preparations a gastric mill rhythm was evoked at 11 and 15 C, with the pacemaker active and with AB/PD hyperpolarized; at 19 and 21 C only a subset produced one.
outcomes.source: Results, Gastric mill rhythms can be evoked when the pyloric pacemaker is suppressed, paragraph 2; Figure 4, figure supplement 2d
outcomes.quote: Figure 4—figure supplement 2d shows that in all nine preparations, the gastric mill rhythm was activated at 11°C and 15°C, whereas at 19°C and 21°C only a subset of preparations produced gastric mill rhythms at these elevated temperatures
outcomes.notes: As fig4s2-gastric-without-pyloric-pacemaker; the PD-hyperpolarized set is not in the record.

outcomes.statement: In the example preparation the ratio of LG to PD period is close to an integer at both temperatures, about 10 at 7 C and about 11 at 23 C, and PD bursts end shortly before LG bursts start.
outcomes.source: Results, Integer coupling is maintained across a physiological temperature range, paragraph 2; Figure 5a
outcomes.quote: The ratio of LG to PD periods was close to an integer at both temperatures (~10 at 7°C and ~11 at 23°C)
outcomes.notes: Reading (a), the LG cycle closest to the labelled T_LG; at 7 C (file 0006, 6.92 C) T_LG 9.244 s, mean T_PD 0.843 s, ratio 10.961 (0.04 from an integer); at 23 C (file 0079, 23.07 C) T_LG 3.438 s, mean T_PD 0.316 s, ratio 10.873 (0.13 from an integer). A second 7 C cycle with T_LG 9.245 s has mean T_PD 0.923 s and ratio 10.016, closer to the label's 0.911 s and 10.06. Reading (b), the median ratio of the file, gives 10.76 and 14.02 and misses. LG bursts start a median 0.17 s (7 C) and 0.13 s (23 C) after the last PD burst end; this part of the statement is shown, not judged.

outcomes.statement: LG and PD burst periods are significantly integer-coupled at every temperature from 7 to 21 C (two-sample Kolmogorov-Smirnov test against shuffled periods, p < 1e-5, D > 0.24).
outcomes.source: Results, Integer coupling is maintained across a physiological temperature range, paragraph 4; Figure 5b, 5d and 5e
outcomes.quote: LG and PD were significantly integer-coupled, at temperatures from 7°C to 21°C (p < 10 –5 , D > 0.24)

statistics.test: two-sample Kolmogorov-Smirnoff test, observed against shuffled significands, per temperature
statistics.n: LG bursts pooled across all 10 preparations at each temperature

outcomes.notes: With the code's shuffle (100 draws, reading a) every bin from 7 to 21 C has median p below 0.05/9 (1.5e-8 to 4.9e-4) and median D above 0.216 (0.223 at 21 C to 0.351), Methods burst rule. D at 21 C under the five seeds is 0.2233, 0.2239, 0.2207, 0.2221 and 0.2214, all above the bound, so the outcome does not depend on the seed. The reported p < 1e-5 is not met at 17 and 21 C with the code's draws (median p 2.6e-5 and 4.9e-4). With the permutation shuffle (reading b) every bin from 7 to 21 C has p below 1e-5 but D at 21 C is 0.199. 23 C is not significant (D 0.162, p 0.31). The code's burst rule gives the same results within 0.01 in D. The criterion's reproduced clause (p < 0.05/9, D > 0.216) is applied; whether the reported p < 1e-5 should decide instead, under which no reading meets both bounds, is asked of a reader (questions/powell-2021.yaml).
deviations: The paper used one shuffle draw per temperature; here the median D and p over 1000 draws are reported, as the criterion sets. p is the asymptotic p of MATLAB's kstest2.

outcomes.statement: DG and PD burst periods are not significantly integer-coupled at any temperature (p > 0.02, D < 0.16).
outcomes.source: Results, Integer coupling is maintained across a physiological temperature range, paragraph 4; Figure 5c, 5d and 5e
outcomes.quote: while DG and PD were not significantly coupled at any temperature (p > 0.02, D < 0.16)

statistics.test: two-sample Kolmogorov-Smirnoff test, observed against shuffled significands, per temperature

outcomes.notes: With the code's shuffle no bin reaches p < 0.05/9 (median p 0.082 to 0.925, D 0.115 to 0.160, Methods burst rule); the smallest p over bins is 0.078 to 0.084 under the five seeds. D is below 0.16 except at 23 C (12 DG cycles, D 0.160, or 0.19 with the code's burst rule). With the permutation shuffle (variant) the 11 and 15 C bins are significant (p 5.1e-4 and 5.8e-4, D 0.084 and 0.104), so the absence rests on the code's shuffle, which the criterion names. 901_005 has no DG spikes, so nine preparations enter.

outcomes.statement: The area between the significand c.d.f. and the diagonal, a measure of integer coupling, is larger for LG/PD than for DG/PD at every temperature, and the DG/PD areas overlap those of shuffled periods.
outcomes.source: Results, Integer coupling is maintained across a physiological temperature range, paragraph 4; Figure 5e
outcomes.quote: Areas for LG/PD significands were larger than areas for DG/PD significands at every temperature ( Figure 5e ), suggesting greater integer coupling. Areas for DG/PD significands overlapped with areas computed after shuffling
outcomes.notes: The LG area exceeds the DG area in all 8 bins where both exist (LG 0.127 to 0.193, DG 0.050 to 0.079) under all five seeds. The DG area (mean plus or minus SEM over preparations) overlaps the shuffled area in 1 of 8 bins under the claim's seed (7 C) and 1, 4, 2, 2 and 1 of 8 under the five seeds, never in most; in every other bin the DG area lies above the shuffled one. Against the shuffle of the LG call (the other gray line), DG overlaps in 3 of 8. With the code's burst rule, 2 of 7. Over the six bins with more than one DG preparation (where the SEM is defined), DG overlaps in 1 of 6 under the claim's seed and 1, 4, 2, 2 and 1 of 6 under the five seeds. With the shuffled pool built from independent draws in place of one permutation, 3, 2, 3, 3 and 3 of 8.
deviations: Bins with a single preparation have no SEM; their interval is taken as the value itself (the code draws them without an error bar).

outcomes.statement: The ratio of LG to PD cycle period does not change with temperature (Spearman test, p = 0.88, n = 3799).
outcomes.source: Results, Integer coupling is maintained across a physiological temperature range, paragraph 4; Figure 5f
outcomes.quote: Ratios of LG to PD cycle period were spread across a similar range of temperatures, even at higher temperatures when integer coupling was less pronounced (p = 0.88, n = 3799 , PD cycles pooled across all preparations, Spearman test)
outcomes.notes: Spearman over all cycles, rho = 0.016, p = 0.311, n = 3850 (Methods burst rule); with the code's burst rule rho = 0.002, p = 0.880, n = 3799, the paper's numbers. Prep-by-prep means per bin, rho = 0.21, p = 0.10 (64 means).

outcomes.statement: At low temperatures the ratios of LG to PD cycle period range widely, from about 5 to 25.
outcomes.source: Results, Integer coupling is maintained across a physiological temperature range, paragraph 4; Figure 5f
outcomes.quote: At low temperatures, when integer coupling was particularly strong (as seen from the horizontal banding), these ratios were distributed over a wide range from 5 to 25
outcomes.notes: Reading (a), 7 C bin, 283 ratios; 2.5th and 97.5th percentiles 7.04 and 26.03 (minimum 5.76, maximum 39.91, 1st percentile 6.81). Reading (b), 7 to 11 C, 1609 ratios; 7.03 and 25.99 (1st percentile 6.07). Both lie within 4.5 to 27.5 but neither reaches down to 5.5, so the lower end of the bulk is about 7, not 5. The code's burst rule gives the same percentiles within 0.05.

outcomes.statement: LG burst starts are phase-locked to the PD cycle, their distribution in PD phase sharply peaked and significantly non-uniform (Rayleigh test, p < 4e-4, 7.5 < z < 45).
outcomes.source: Results, LG preserves phase locking to PD across physiological temperatures, paragraph 2; Figure 6a and 6b
outcomes.quote: LG burst start probabilities were sharply peaked ( Figure 6b ) and were significantly different from a uniform distribution ( Figure 6b , dashed line, p < 4×10 –4 , 7.5<z<45, Rayleigh test for non-uniformity; see Methods for details)

statistics.test: Rayleigh test for non-uniformity, per preparation and temperature

outcomes.notes: Methods sample (a), first 40 starts, 41 preparation and temperature combinations; all p < 0.05 (largest 0.008), 4 combinations not below 4.4e-4, z 4.74 to 35.77 (Methods burst rule). With the code's burst rule one combination has p = 0.082. The later code's sample (b), first 50, gives p up to 2.1e-4 and z 8.20 to 45.31 (Methods burst rule, within the bounds) and p up to 4.5e-4 and z 7.49 to 45.44 (code's burst rule), the reported p < 4e-4 and 7.5 < z < 45 within rounding. The archived code's pooled sample (c) gives z 67 to 577. Burst starts at even rounded temperatures (220 of 4128 LG starts with a PD phase) belong to no bin and are not tested. Whether the first-50 sample, which matches the reported ranges, should be the main reading is asked of a reader (questions/powell-2021.yaml).
deviations: The reported ranges match the sample of the later code (commit 7a82b1f, first 50 starts), not the Methods' first 40, as the claims file anticipated; the outcome follows the Methods, as the criterion sets.

outcomes.statement: A total of 3816 LG burst starts and 3228 DG burst starts across nine temperature points and 10 preparations enter the phase distributions, and about 35% of preparation and temperature combinations have fewer than 40 burst starts.
outcomes.source: Materials and methods, Analysis of distribution of LG/DG burst starts in PD phase, paragraph 2
outcomes.quote: Preparation and temperature combinations where there were <40 burst starts (~35% of data) were excluded. A total of n = 3816 LG burst starts and n = 3228 DG burst starts across nine temperature points and 10 preparations are plotted in Figure 6b,d
outcomes.notes: Partially reproduced: two of the three quantities are within tolerance. Methods burst rule, all starts with a defined PD phase in the bins 7 to 23 C; LG 3908 (within 3816 plus or minus 381.6), DG 3573 (above 3228 plus or minus 322.8 by 22). Fraction of combinations with fewer than 40 starts, reading (a), over combinations with any start, 0.339 (LG), 0.386 (DG), 0.361 (both); over all 90 per neuron 0.54 to 0.61; reading (b), of starts, 0.086 to 0.100. With the code's burst rule the totals are LG 3865 and DG 3448, both within tolerance, and with the code's burst rule and the archived code's sample (temperatures with at least 100 pooled starts) LG 3816, the paper's number, and DG 3220. Starts at even rounded temperatures, in none of the nine temperature points, are not counted (220 LG and 218 DG). Whether the code's burst rule, with which the paper's counts match, should decide is asked of a reader (questions/powell-2021.yaml).
deviations: The claims file's reading (a) does not say over which combinations the fraction is taken; both those with any start and all 90 are shown. The outcome is decided by the DG total, whichever is used.

outcomes.statement: From 7 to 21 C, LG bursts start at a phase of about 0.5 in the PD cycle, and this phase does not trend with temperature (Spearman test, p = 0.46, rho = -0.31).
outcomes.source: Results, LG preserves phase locking to PD across physiological temperatures, paragraph 2; Figure 6b inset
outcomes.quote: From 7°C to 21°C, LG bursts started at a phase of ~0.5 in the PD cycle ( Figure 6b , inset), and this phase offset did not significantly trend across this temperature range (p = 0.46, ρ = –0.31, Spearman test)

statistics.n: 8 temperature steps (7 to 21 C), means across preparations

outcomes.notes: No trend from 7 to 21 C; all starts, rho = -0.190, p = 0.651; first 40, rho = -0.429, p = 0.289 (Methods burst rule). With the code's burst rule and all starts, rho = -0.310, p = 0.456, the paper's values. The bin means (all starts) are 0.416 to 0.494, mean 0.45, with 7, 9, 17 and 21 C below 0.45; first 40, 0.337 to 0.504. The phase part fails under both samples, the trend part holds under both.

outcomes.statement: LG spike probability in the PD cycle shows a pronounced decrease at higher temperatures, occurring close to PD burst termination.
outcomes.source: Results, LG preserves phase locking to PD across physiological temperatures, paragraph 3; Figure 6c
outcomes.quote: We measured the spike probability of LG conditional on PD phase across this temperature range and found a pronounced decrease in the probability of spiking in LG at higher temperatures ( Figure 6c ). This decrease in LG spike probability occurred close to PD burst termination
outcomes.notes: The LG spike p.d.f. at the mean PD burst-end phase (about 0.19 to 0.22) is below 1 at every temperature with at least 1000 spikes (reading a, 0.45 to 0.81 from 7 to 21 C, 0.23 at 23 C), but its Spearman correlation with temperature is positive (reading a, rho = 0.150, p = 0.70; reading b, 0.167, p = 0.67; without 23 C, 0.64 and 0.67). The value rises from 0.62 at 11 C to 0.81 at 21 C; only the 23 C bin, from the two preparations that reach it, shows a low value. The code's burst rule gives the same picture. The odd-temperature filter leaves out 3.6% of LG spikes with a PD phase (even rounded temperatures).

outcomes.statement: DG bursts are not phase-locked to PD; DG burst starts are not sharply peaked in PD phase, not significantly non-uniform in every preparation and temperature, and the effect is much smaller than for LG (p from 0.001 to 0.85, 0.15 < z < 13).
outcomes.source: Results, LG preserves phase locking to PD across physiological temperatures, paragraph 4; Figure 6d and 6e
outcomes.quote: DG burst starts are not sharply peaked in PD phase, and they are not significantly different from a uniform distribution for all preparations at all temperatures ( Figure 6e , p ∈ [0.001, 0.85], 0.15 < z < 13, Rayleigh test)

statistics.test: Rayleigh test for non-uniformity, per preparation and temperature

outcomes.notes: Methods sample (first 40), 35 DG combinations; 16 with p >= 0.05, median z 3.38 against 22.59 for LG (Methods burst rule). DG p 1.4e-8 to 0.82 and z 0.21 to 16.25, beyond the reported 0.001 to 0.85 and 0.15 to 13 at the significant end; with the first 50, z 0.16 to 12.27 (Methods burst rule) or 13.65 (code's), p from 2.3e-6 to 0.85.

outcomes.statement: DG spike probability does not show a noticeable decrease close to the end of PD bursting.
outcomes.source: Results, LG preserves phase locking to PD across physiological temperatures, paragraph 4; Figure 6f
outcomes.quote: DG spike probability also does not show a noticeable decrease close to the end of PD bursting
outcomes.notes: At the eight temperatures with at least 1000 DG spikes (7 to 21 C) the DG p.d.f. at the PD burst-end bin is 0.888 to 1.089, above 1 minus half the LG drop at every one (thresholds 0.725 to 0.906). The same holds under the code's burst rule (0.912 to 1.089). The odd-temperature filter leaves out 9.2% of DG spikes with a PD phase (even rounded temperatures).

findings.statement: The record holds spike annotations and raw data only for the evoked preparations. The nine preparations with spontaneous gastric mill rhythms (Figure 2 and its supplement) and the nine with the pyloric pacemaker hyperpolarized (Figure 4, figure supplement 2) are not in it, although the paper's data statement names only this record for its raw data and spike annotations. Four of the paper's findings cannot be tested.

941_003.zip and 941_006.zip hold raw ABF recordings of two preparations recorded on 11 and 12 June 2019 (ABF header dates), with no spike annotations and no description. Neither is among the ten evoked preparations of evoked_data.mat, and they belong to none of the three sets the Methods describe (2013, 2017, 2020). 941_006 is one of the four preparations of Figure 3, figure supplement 1, so that claim can be tested only on the other three.
There is no zip of raw recordings for 901_005, one of the ten evoked preparations; its spike times, temperature and mask are in evoked_data.mat.

The record has no README and its description is the paper's abstract. The fields of evoked_data.mat are not described; the mask (0 in runs of about 7 s, stimulation by the paper's code) and the 1 kHz sampling of temperature and mask are evident only from the values and the code. The preparation and file names are MATLAB categorical objects, readable outside MATLAB only by decoding the file's MCOS subsystem, and the fields T and time_offset are empty in every preparation. Zenodo types the record as a journal article, not a dataset.

932_151, one of the ten evoked preparations, was recorded on 2 May 2019 by the header of 932_151_0000.abf, while the Methods say the evoked preparations came from crabs caught in 2017. 901_046 and 901_098 carry 2017 dates as described.

Seven zips hold raw recordings as crabsort .crab files and four as ABF files. The .crab zip of 901_062 holds 101 files, while evoked_data.mat stacks 58 files of that preparation; the other zips hold as many files as are stacked.

In the data, 9 of the 10 evoked preparations have an LG rhythm at every temperature step from 7 to 21 C at which they were held, as the paper says, when 901_062, whose last step was 19 C, is counted; 901_086 was held and stimulated at 21 C for 330 s with no LG spike. The record does not say why 901_062 stopped at 19 C.

evoked_data.mat matches the paper's analysis. Its ten preparations are those of getEvokedData.m, no recording is deposited twice, the stimulation mask and LG spikes and the temperature and PD spikes share their clocks, and with the code's burst rule and computations the paper's reported numbers are obtained exactly (Q10 paired t-test t = 1.27, p = 0.235; 3799 cycles and Spearman p = 0.88 in Figure 5f; LG phase trend rho = -0.31, p = 0.46; 3816 LG burst starts).

The DG spike times in evoked_data.mat are not sorted in nine of the ten preparations (1 to 50 times per preparation, 129 in all, a spike time is smaller than the one before it); the PD and LG spike times are sorted. The paper's code (getEvokedData.m) sorts PD and LG on loading but not DG; taking DG in the file's order changes the DG bursts of the code's rule by -2 to +6 per preparation (3675 against 3667 in all). This attempt sorts all three.

disagreements.reason: On the criterion's literal wording. Cell 16 reports 8 of 10, failing 901_062 and 901_086, but the code also requires bins 7 and 21 to be present, which the criterion does not ask. 901_062 never reaches 21 C (0 s, T_max 19.3) and has bursts in every bin it was held at, so the literal reading gives 9 of 10. If 21 C must be reached, it is 8 of 10, which would fail the tolerance of 0. The added requirement is not stated as an assumption, and both counts should be reported. The Methods' 'in some preparations, 19 C was the warmest' fits two preparations topping out at 19 C. It could not check whether 901_062's run stopped at 19 C because no rhythm could be evoked at 21 C, and asked for a printout of 901_062's stimulation blocks and temperatures at the end of the recording.

Cell 43, Methods rule: LG 3908 (in tolerance) and fraction 0.339 (in tolerance), but DG 3573 exceeds 3228 + 322.8. With the code rule all three pass, and pooling temperatures with >= 100 gives exactly LG 3816. The fraction under reading (a) is taken over combinations with at least one start (0.339); over all 90 it would be 0.544, a choice not stated as an assumption, though both are shown.

paper_notes.statement: The Methods keep bursts of at least n spikes (5 for LG and DG, 2 for PD), but the paper's burst detection, crabsort.computePeriods, compares n with the number of inter-spike intervals in a burst, keeping bursts of at least n + 1 spikes. The paper's reported numbers follow the code's rule (for example 3799 cycles in Figure 5f, against 3850 under the Methods' rule, and 3228 DG burst starts, which the Methods' rule exceeds by more than 10%).

The Methods test the first 40 LG and DG burst starts of each preparation and temperature for non-uniformity, but the reported ranges (LG p < 4e-4, 7.5 < z < 45; DG z up to 13) are those of the first 50, the sample of the later code (marderlab/gastric commit 7a82b1f). The archived commit the paper cites (fa07d36) pools all starts of a temperature over preparations, which gives z of 67 to 577. With 40 starts z cannot exceed 40.

The Methods compute the Q10 from the mean burst frequency at each temperature against 11 C, but fig_burst_period.m computes a Q10 for every burst at its own temperature, against the bursts within 0.1 C of 11 C, removes Q10s above 10 and averages per preparation. The reported count of 8 of 10 preparations near 2 and the paired t-test (t = 1.27, p = 0.235) follow the code; the Methods' formula gives 1 to 3 of 10 and LG Q10s up to 39 from temperatures crossed during ramps.

Figure 3, figure supplement 1 says that 4 of the 10 evoked preparations had spontaneous rhythms, but one of the four preparations its script uses (941_006) is not among the ten evoked preparations and was recorded in June 2019, not 2017. In evoked_data.mat, 3 of the 10 evoked preparations (901_062, 901_080, 901_086) have LG bursting before their first stimulation at 11 C, which with 941_006 makes the four of the script. A fourth of the ten, 932_151, has 16 LG burst periods before stimulation at 9.83 to 9.93 C, so the paper's 4 of 10 may count it in place of 941_006.

The paper says rhythms were evoked 'across a temperature range of 7 to 21 C in 9 of 10 preparations', with steps of 2 or 4 C 'until a gastric mill rhythm could no longer be evoked'. It does not say whether a preparation whose warmest step was 19 C (901_062, never brought to 21 C) counts among the nine, nor whether temperatures crossed only between steps (9, 13 and 17 C for most preparations) count. The attempt assumed that only bins held at least 2 minutes count and that a preparation passes with a rhythm at every step it had, which gives the paper's 9; requiring 21 C gives 8, and counting every bin crossed gives 3. Which did the authors count?

entries.name: powell-2021
entries.title: Coupling of the gastric mill and pyloric rhythms across temperature (Powell et al. 2021)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Powell, Haddad, Gorur-Shandilya and Marder (2021) on Zenodo record 3924718, which holds the spike times, temperature and stimulation mask of the ten preparations in which gastric mill rhythms were evoked, and raw recordings. It tests the temperature dependence of the LG and PD burst periods, their Q10s, the slowing after stimulation, integer coupling of LG and DG with PD, and the phase of LG and DG in the PD cycle. The spontaneous recordings and those with the pyloric pacemaker hyperpolarized are not in the record.
